paper_id: Distributed Redundant Placement for Microservice-based Applications at the Edge
title: Distributed Redundant Placement for Microservice-based Applications at the Edge
motivation: Kubernetes healing capability is insufficient for high availability under edge heterogeneity and variability; current service placement research ignores composite service structure
problem_framing: Stochastic discrete optimization to decide for each microservice candidate how many instances and on which edge sites to place them
key_insight: Redundancy allowing one candidate dispatched to multiple edge sites alleviates single-site bottleneck risk and balances requests from different end users
method_signature: SAA-RP framework with GA-based Server Selection (GASS) algorithm for sequential combinatorial microservice structure
evaluation_criteria: Overall response time minimization under heterogeneous SBS capacity constraints using real-world EUA dataset
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: Redundancy is not always a win; creating too many instances can lead to unacceptably high response times and even instability
evidence_for_taste: the default assignment does not fully take heterogeneity
redundancy is not always a win
the outage time could be dozens of minutes
thinking_moves: 将复合微服务的组合结构纳入边缘部署建模
通过随机采样(SAA)将随机优化问题转为确定性子问题
用遗传算法求解每个采样实例以规避组合爆炸
从生产实践出发,指出Kubernetes默认调度器的不足
承认冗余策略存在危险性,需权衡实例数量
cites_own_work: Deploying data-intensive applications with multiple services components on edge (2019)
